requirement_title: Feature Request: Allow generation of Formatter for a type in a referenced assembly
requirement_text:
# REQ-2129: Feature Request: Allow generation of Formatter for a type in a referenced assembly

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2129
Type: feature

## Requirement

Given Project A (contains `ProjectA.MyType`, has no and cannot have a reference to the MessagePack NuGet package) and Project B (references Project A and MessagePack), the reporter needs a source-generated `IMessagePackFormatter` for `ProjectA.MyType` generated inside Project B.

Proposed solution: add a `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]` attribute that works for partial classes implementing `IMessagePackFormatter<T>`:

```csharp
[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]
partial class MyObjectFormatter: IMessagePackFormatter<MyObject>;
```

The class does not need a body; the implementation is source-generated by `MessagePack.SourceGenerator.MessagePackGenerator` as usual.

For attribute-based property keys and other settings (such as Union), the issue lists three alternatives: (1) use `System.Runtime.Serialization.DataMember` and related attributes; (2) let the generator and analyzers work with user-defined copies of the MessagePack attributes; (3) source-generate the attributes themselves via `RegisterPostInitializationOutput`.

Motivation: Project A is a NuGet library that should stay minimal with zero dependencies.

## Acceptance criteria

- A `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]` attribute exists and can be applied to a partial class implementing `IMessagePackFormatter<T>`.
- The source generator emits the formatter implementation for `T` inside the annotated class, in the assembly that declares the class (Project B), even when `T` is declared in a referenced assembly.
- The annotated class may be declared without a body (`partial class X : IMessagePackFormatter<T>;`).
- `T` needs no MessagePack attributes: without `[DataContract]` or `[MessagePackObject]` on `T` the generated formatter uses contractless behaviour over public members. (derived from maintainer comment)
- If `T` does carry MessagePack attributes, they are honoured. (derived from maintainer comment)
- Private members are not required to be serialized; only public members are in scope. (derived from maintainer comment)
- Project A needs no reference to the MessagePack package. (derived)

## Notes from discussion

- AArnott: "We might simplistically say this only works in 'contractless' mode, such that you need no attributes on it at all. If there are attributes on it, fine, we'll use them. But if there is no `[DataContract]` or `[MessagePackObject]` attribute on the type, go contractless by default."
- AArnott on prerequisite: "Does ProjectA.MyType requires only `public` members to be serialized? That seems a prerequisite for anything here." Reporter: yes.
- AArnott is not a fan of a `PropertyKeys` dictionary on the formatter, and warns that copying attributes into Project A breaks reflection-based (dynamic resolver) mode.
- AArnott suggested a surrogate-type design: `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter(SurrogateType = typeof(ProjectASurrogate))]`, keys mapped by property name; reporter: "Looks good." No design was settled in the thread.

findings.claim: The requirement says that if T carries MessagePack attributes they are honoured; the change never reads them. When no SurrogateType is given, CreateContractlessMembers runs unconditionally. It ignores [MessagePackObject], [Key], [IgnoreMember], [DataContract], [DataMember] and [IgnoreDataMember] on T and serializes every public read-write member under its CLR name. As a result, a member marked [IgnoreMember] (e.g. a secret) is still serialized. Custom string keys and int keys on T are also replaced by member names, so the wire format differs from what the dynamic resolver produces for the same type. The README and attribute docs describe this always-contractless behaviour, which contradicts the requirement.

The formatted type ProjectA.Keyed comes from a referenced assembly and is [MessagePackObject] with [IgnoreMember] Secret and [Key("custom_name")] Name. IgnoredMemberOfAttributedTypeIsNotSerialized fails on head because the generated source contains 'Secret'. StringKeyOfAttributedTypeIsHonoured fails on head because 'custom_name' is absent.

hunches.claim: The requirement says MessagePack attributes on T must be honoured, but they are ignored. When SurrogateType is null, Collect always calls CreateContractlessMembers(type). It never checks [MessagePackObject], [Key], [IgnoreMember], [DataContract] or [DataMember] on T. Example: T is [MessagePackObject] with [Key(0)] int Value and [IgnoreMember] int Ignored. The generated formatter still writes a string-keyed map that includes 'Ignored', so the wire format differs from what T's own attributes declare.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.GeneratedFormatterHonoursAttributesTests. The formatted type comes from a referenced assembly and has [MessagePackObject], [Key(0)] and [IgnoreMember]. Assert the generated MyObjectFormatter source does not mention 'Ignored' and does not use WriteMapHeader. Both assertions fail on head. (generated tests: IgnoreMemberOnFormattedTypeIsHonoured, IntKeysOnFormattedTypeAreHonoured)

hunches.claim: GetInstanceMembers keeps only the first (most derived) symbol of each name and then filters with IsPublicReadWrite. If a derived class overrides only the getter (public override int X => ...), Roslyn exposes no SetMethod on the override, so X is filtered out. The base read-write X is skipped by the name check. The same happens when a derived non-public member hides a public base member. The property is then silently left out of the contractless contract.

receipt_plan.detail: Drive CSharpGeneratorDriver on: class Base { public virtual int X { get; set; } } class Derived : Base { public override int X { get => 1; } }, with [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] partial class F : IMessagePackFormatter<Derived>. Assert the generated F source references 'X'; on head it does not.

hunches.claim: The ForAttributeWithMetadataName predicate accepts only ClassDeclarationSyntax. A 'partial record F : IMessagePackFormatter<T>' marked with the attribute therefore produces no implementation and no MsgPack019/020 diagnostic. The user sees only CS0535 (missing interface members).

receipt_plan.detail: VerifyCS test with [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] partial record F : IMessagePackFormatter<MyObj> { } using LanguageVersion.Latest. Observe CS0535 errors and no MsgPack diagnostic.

hunches.claim: The generator hook-up in GeneratorUtilities excludes [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] classes from the hand-written formatter registration only by matching the attribute's display name. The user-declared formatter is still registered as an ObjectSerializationInfo in the resolver. Existing users who already have a hand-written formatter with this attribute name cannot be affected, but the new `partial class` emission means the generated class declaration omits the user's accessibility, modifiers and type constraints. For an `internal sealed partial` or `public sealed` user formatter this would produce CS0262 or CS0263 conflicts, and for a formatter with its own base class the generated declaration will conflict. The generated declaration also repeats the interface list, which is allowed, but a mismatch in the sealed or static modifiers is a compile error in the user's project.

receipt_plan.detail: Add a snapshot test with `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] public sealed partial class F : IMessagePackFormatter<ProjectA.T>;`, and check that the generated output compiles without CS0262/CS0263 or other modifier-conflict errors.

hunches.claim: The contractless mode differs from the real ContractlessStandardResolver. It serializes only public read-write members, skips get-only properties and readonly fields, sorts the members ordinally, and uses no constructor. It also flags the keys as string keys with the intKey index set to the sorted position. Wire bytes from this formatter would differ from `MessagePackSerializer` with ContractlessStandardResolver for the same type, for example by dropping get-only members. Users who migrate from the contractless resolver to the generated formatter would notice the difference. The ledger says to follow the requirement here, and the requirement only says 'public members', so this is an unresolved gap.

receipt_plan.detail: Use a class `T { public int A {get;set;} public int B {get;} public readonly int C; }`. Serialize an instance with ContractlessStandardResolver and with the generated formatter, then compare the bytes: the get-only B and readonly C will be missing.

hunches.claim: A user's type T that does carry [MessagePackObject]/[Key] attributes is not honoured. The collector ignores T's own attributes and always uses contractless member names, so integer keys, [IgnoreMember] and custom formatters on T are dropped. The requirement says attributes on T must be honoured.

receipt_plan.detail: Define `[MessagePackObject] class T { [Key(0)] public int A {get;set;} [IgnoreMember] public int B {get;set;} }` and a generated formatter for it. Serialize an instance with the dynamic resolver and with the generated formatter. The bytes differ: map with string keys versus array.

hunches.claim: The requirement says that if T carries MessagePack attributes, they are honoured. The collector ignores [MessagePackObject], [Key], and [DataContract] on T and always uses contractless mode or the surrogate. The README and attribute docs do not say that T's own attributes are ignored.

receipt_plan.detail: Define a type in the test assembly with [MessagePackObject] and [Key(0)] on two members, add [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] for it, and assert the bytes are an array with integer keys. The current code emits a string-key map.

hunches.claim: Requirement says that if T carries MessagePack attributes they are honoured, but the collector ignores T's own [Key]/[MessagePackObject]/[DataContract] attributes entirely. No test covers a T with attributes, so deleting or adding that behaviour changes nothing in the suite.

receipt_plan.detail: Add an ExecutionTests case with a T carrying [MessagePackObject]/[Key(n)] on its members and a formatter marked [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] with no surrogate. Assert that the output uses integer keys. Expected to fail because CreateContractlessMembers always emits string keys.

hunches.claim: The partial-class guard (IsPartial), the MsgPack019 path, and the NoDeserializingConstructor path for a class with no accessible parameterless constructor have no coverage that would catch their removal. The diagnostic tests cover MsgPack019 only for a non-partial class. The no-default-constructor branch has no test at all, so deleting it survives.

hunches.claim: No test covers the IsPublicReadWrite filter on fields (public fields, readonly fields, const fields) or on non-public setters. ExternalPerson has a get-only property only, and the fixtures have no fields. Mutating the field branch (for example dropping `!field.IsReadOnly`) survives.

SurrogateControlsKeysAndMembership uses only int keys, and the Tests project covers only the mixed-key diagnostic. hunches.claim: The GeneratorUtilities filter that excludes [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] classes from the hand-written formatter registration has no direct test. GeneratedFormattersAreRegisteredInGeneratedResolver checks only the resolved formatter type. A double-registration would likely cause a duplicate-case compile error, but nothing asserts it. There are no generator snapshot tests for the new output, so the template change for user-declared formatters (`partial class`) is verified only by compilation.

hunches.claim: The surrogate test checks only the array header length (8) and that Internal deserializes to 0. It never checks that Id lands at index 3 or Name at index 7, so swapping the key mapping or ignoring the IntKey would survive.

receipt_plan.detail: GeneratedFormatterCollector.cs:182 swap: `CreateMember(target, intKey: intKey, ...)` -> `intKey: members.Count`; a round-trip plus array-length assertion still passes if MaxKey stays 7, so it is likely to survive unless slot positions are asserted.

hunches.claim: GeneratorUtilities now drops [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] classes from the known-formatter set, so T is no longer a known formatted type for TypeCollector. Suppose T is declared in the same compilation without [MessagePackObject] and used as a member of another [MessagePackObject] type. That member then hits the MsgPack003 path and its resolver registration, although a formatter for T exists. Metadata T is only spared because of the L11 early return.

interpretations.label: A
interpretations.summary: 'Contractless behaviour over public members' means only public read-write instance properties and fields are serialized. Get-only properties and readonly fields are skipped, and deserialization always uses a parameterless constructor. This is what CreateContractlessMembers and IsPublicReadWrite implement.

interpretations.label: B
interpretations.summary: 'Contractless behaviour' means matching ContractlessStandardResolver. Public get-only properties and readonly fields are also serialized (IsReadable=true, IsWritable=false), and on deserialization they are set via a constructor whose parameters match by name. This requires CreateContractlessMembers to include public readable members, a constructor-matching step filling constructorParameters, and relaxing the parameterless-constructor requirement at GeneratedFormatterCollector.cs:77.
